headline: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce get married

chunks.text: Taylor Swift, [[one of the most]] famous singers in the world, has married the American football star Travis Kelce. [[According to news reports]], the [[ceremony]] was held at Madison Square Garden, a huge [[arena]] in New York City. Hundreds of fans {{turned up}} outside, [[hoping]] to see the two stars. For weeks, people had {{looked forward to}} [[the big day]].

verbs.wrong: To wait for many hours to see someone
verbs.why: Turn up means to arrive somewhere, often without a fixed appointment. Hundreds of fans turned up outside the arena, hoping to catch a glimpse of the couple.

verbs.wrong: To make careful plans for a special day
verbs.correct: To feel excited about something in the future
verbs.why: Look forward to means to feel excited about something before it happens. For weeks, fans had looked forward to the wedding, eager to see how it would go.

chunks.text: Just before the wedding, the couple {{gave away}} a large amount of money. Reports say they {{handed out}} about 26 million dollars to 20 different [[charities]], [[including]] [[food banks]] and children's hospitals. Many people [[praised]] the pair for being so [[generous]] and for {{giving back}} to [[those in need]]. News of the [[donation]] [[spread]] quickly online.

verbs.wrong: To share the cost of something with others
verbs.correct: To give something to others for free
verbs.why: Give away means to give something to someone without asking for money in return. The couple gave away about 26 million dollars to charities before their own wedding.

verbs.wrong: To lend money that must be repaid
verbs.correct: To give something to many people
verbs.why: Hand out means to distribute something so that many separate people each receive a share. Reports say the couple handed out about 26 million dollars across 20 charities.

verbs.wrong: To stop refusing and finally agree
verbs.correct: To do something good for others in return
verbs.why: Give back means to do something helpful for others, often because you feel fortunate yourself. Fans praised the pair for giving back so generously to those in need.

chunks.text: A lot of famous people {{showed up}} for the wedding. The actor Tom Hanks, the director Steven Spielberg, and the football player Tom Brady all {{took part in}} the celebration. The singer Selena Gomez, [[a close friend]] of Swift, was a [[bridesmaid]]. According to reports, the [[former]] Beatle Paul McCartney even {{teamed up with}} Swift and the singer Stevie Nicks to perform a song.

verbs.wrong: To be seen by news cameras
verbs.correct: To arrive or attend an event
verbs.why: Show up means to arrive at an event, especially one people were waiting for. Many famous guests showed up for the wedding at Madison Square Garden.

verbs.wrong: To be a special guest at an event
verbs.correct: To be involved in an activity with others
verbs.why: Take part in means to join an activity along with other people. Tom Hanks and Tom Brady both took part in the celebration that night.

verbs.wrong: To sing a song for someone special
verbs.why: Team up with means to join another person to do something together. Paul McCartney teamed up with Swift and Stevie Nicks to perform a song at the reception.

chunks.text: The wedding {{went ahead}} [[without any problems]], and the party {{carried on}} [[late into the night]]. Some [[guests]] said the evening {{turned out}} to be one of the most [[magical]] they had ever seen. For many fans, though, the huge gift to charity {{stood out}} the most. They hope other rich stars will follow the couple's [[example]].

verbs.wrong: To make progress in your career
verbs.correct: To happen or continue as planned
verbs.why: Go ahead means an event happens as it was planned, with nothing stopping it. The wedding went ahead without any problems, exactly as the couple had hoped.
Carry on means to continue doing something without stopping. The wedding party carried on late into the night.

verbs.wrong: To be planned down to the last detail
verbs.correct: To finally become a certain way
verbs.why: Turn out means something becomes clear as a final result, sometimes better or worse than expected. Some guests said the evening turned out to be one of the most magical nights they had seen.

verbs.wrong: To break a world record for donations
verbs.correct: To be the most noticeable thing
verbs.why: Stand out means to be the one detail people notice and remember most. For many fans, the couple's huge gift to charity stood out even more than the wedding itself.

mainIdea.s: Two American stars married at a New York arena, and the party carried on late into the night. For many fans, the best part was the 26 million dollars the couple gave to charity.
mainIdea.why: The couple handed out about 26 million dollars to 20 charities before the ceremony. For many fans, that gift stood out more than the wedding itself.

mainIdea.s: A singer and a football star married in New York and asked their guests to give to charity instead of gifts. Reports say those guests gave about 26 million dollars in total.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the money came from the couple, not the guests. They also gave it away before the wedding, not in place of presents.

mainIdea.s: A famous football team won a championship game at a packed arena in New York City last weekend. Thousands of fans celebrated in the streets long after the final score.
mainIdea.why: This describes a football championship celebration, a separate event. The article is about Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's wedding and their gift to charity.

tf.s: Even after the wedding was over, fans kept looking forward to the couple's big day.
tf.why: People looked forward to (felt excited about) the wedding for weeks before it happened. You cannot look forward to a day that has already passed.

tf.s: After the ceremony, the party went ahead late into the night.
tf.why: After the ceremony, the party carried on (continued) late into the night. Go ahead means to happen as planned, not to continue for hours.

tf.s: For weeks before the wedding, people had looked forward to the big day.
tf.why: For weeks, people had looked forward to (felt excited about) the wedding.

tf.s: The wedding went ahead without any problems, just as planned.
tf.why: The wedding went ahead (happened as planned) without any problems.

tf.s: Hundreds of fans took part in the wedding outside the arena, hoping to see the two stars.
tf.why: Hundreds of fans turned up (arrived) outside the arena. They did not take part in (join) the wedding, which was held inside.

tf.s: Famous guests such as Tom Hanks and Tom Brady took part in the celebration.
tf.why: The actor Tom Hanks and the football player Tom Brady both took part in (joined) the celebration.
